headline: Your Flexciton waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing semiconductor manufacturers into the right Flexciton planning-and-scheduling offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Anna Robson.
productSummary: Flexciton is a technology company building production planning and scheduling software that helps chipmakers raise efficiency and move toward autonomous operations. Three Flex Apps: Flex Planner turns customer orders into daily wafer-start plans and production schedules with dynamic capacity modeling and mathematical optimization, updated every 45 minutes. Flex Local autonomously schedules lots to tools and balances batching, cycle time, and throughput without rule or parameter tuning. Flex Global connects local schedulers, guides the right WIP to the right toolset, cuts timelink violations, and plans changeover campaigns. Homepage use cases: hidden capacity without new capex, labour efficiency, on-time delivery, cost reduction. Named customers on-site: Seagate Technology, Renesas, Microchip. Intel partnership announced for factory automation and optimisation software. Homepage: 40+ experts dedicated to semiconductor manufacturing optimization, 100+ technical publications, 3 patents in mathematical optimization, 25+ fabs around the world.
coreInsight: Anna already sells autonomous planning and scheduling so chipmakers can uncover hidden capacity, hit commits, and run with fewer scarce engineers. Mila's original pitch is the TAM: scrape semiconductor manufacturers, write to Ops Managers and Production Directors, personalize on operational challenges and AI in the fab, A/B cost reduction versus throughput. The one list is semiconductor manufacturers LinkedIn already lists. The one routing signal is the job-keyword class in their open reqs, because Sales Nav returns that keyword in the same pull and it tells you whether they are staffing wafer-start planning, toolset dispatch, timelink or MES automation, or none of those yet. Ops Manager and Production Director titles are the people layer after the fab is routed. They are not a second TAM. Cost versus throughput is an A/B on the exclusive routes, not a second waterfall.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the keyword already in the job post
sections.takeaway: LinkedIn already names the semiconductor manufacturer and already prints capacity planning, dispatch, MES, or timelink language in the open req. That keyword is stronger than a headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every semiconductor manufacturer
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Planning and wafer-start keywords go first, then toolset scheduling keywords, then timelink and factory-automation keywords, then every remaining in-TAM manufacturer.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each job keyword gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Planning hiring gets a Capacity Commit Brief. Dispatch hiring gets a Toolset KPI Gap Brief. Timelink or MES hiring gets a Fab-Wide Flow Brief. The rest get the Autonomous Fab Playbook, with cost versus throughput as the A/B.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Commit the plan, fill the tool, hold the timelink, skip the firefight
sections.takeaway: The list is always semiconductor manufacturers, aimed at Ops Managers, Production Directors, Fab Managers, and Industrial Engineers. Fab area is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the req they already posted
sections.takeaway: Notice the keyword, poke the spreadsheet or rule-tuning gap that keyword implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the planning keyword first
sections.takeaway: Start where they are already staffing wafer starts and capacity, the problem Flex Planner is built for. Prove reply density, then roll toolset scheduling, timelink automation, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: LinkedIn Sales Nav job search is the TAM Mila already named, semiconductor manufacturers with a visible Ops or Production title, and the planning or scheduling keyword in one pull.

The same pull returns capacity / wafer starts / production control, dispatch / batching / cycle time / reticle, or timelink / MES / CIM / factory automation, which is enough to route without a second enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Flexciton copy: Flex Planner (wafer-start plans updated every 45 minutes), Flex Local (toolset KPIs without rule tuning), Flex Global (timelink constraints and Heatmap), and the remaining autonomous-factory pitch Anna already sells.
Ops Manager, Production Director, and fab area are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last, never the TAM spine.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Planning / wafer-start keyword
tiers.trigger: LinkedIn job post names production planner, capacity planner, wafer starts, industrial engineer, production control, WIP management, capacity modeling, or starts planning. Keyword class estimated, not a Flexciton site field.
tiers.pain: They are staffing the plan. Wafer starts still take days of spreadsheets, so the commit is stale before the shift starts. Flex Planner page: replace days of manual planning with constraint-aware wafer-start plans, delivered autonomously and updated every 45 minutes. No spreadsheets, no firefighting. Customer quote on that page: morning meetings are painful, and shortening them by 15 minutes would be a real ROI.
tiers.valueProp: Flex Planner aligns WIP to customer due dates, turns ERP targets into daily actions, and surfaces Spotlight recommendations such as rescheduling maintenance or qualifying recipes. Planner page: 10% reduction in cycle time at any given WIP level, 30% reduction in standard deviation from target velocity. Homepage Capacity use case: uncover hidden capacity by optimizing how existing tools and resources are used, maximize throughput without new capital investment.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already budgeted a role to keep wafer starts honest against real capacity.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Toolset scheduling keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names dispatcher, scheduler, batching, cycle time, toolset, photolithography scheduling, diffusion scheduling, or reticle, and no planning_capacity keyword. Class estimated.
tiers.pain: They are staffing local dispatch. Rule-based schedulers only hit the KPI for one fab state, then engineers retune. Flex Local page: say goodbye to manual rules and constant parameter tweaking. Comparison table there: legacy solutions consume 50% to 80% of one engineering FTE just to understand and retune at every change in fab state.
tiers.valueProp: Flex Local lets the fab set the objective once. The optimizer balances batching, cycle time, and throughput in real time and pushes shopfloor actions through Runway. Homepage and Flex Local: 9.4% increase in throughput in the photo area, 18% increase in batch size across the diffusion area. Unnamed Flex Local quote: improved moves while reducing risk of reticle breakages, and manufacturing specialists always give positive feedback on the scheduling.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. They already pay people to tune dispatch. The retune loop is the pain Flex Local is built for.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Timelink / factory-automation keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names timelink, Q-time, QTimer, factory automation, MES, CIM, digital twin, Industry 4.0, autonomous factory, or fab-wide scheduling, and no planning_capacity or toolset_scheduling keyword. Class estimated.
tiers.pain: They are staffing the constraint the local dispatcher cannot see. Flex Global page: timelink constraints are too complex for rule-based schedulers. AST blog: when timelinks are violated, wafers require rework or must be scrapped. Heatmap on that page is the congestion view across time and tools, so issues show up before they escalate.
tiers.valueProp: Flex Global connects toolset schedulers, manages timelink constraints, and guides WIP so the right lots arrive for better batching and less scrap. Homepage and Flex Global: 29% reduction in timelink violations in the diffusion area. Mark Patton, Director of Manufacturing, Seagate Technology, on the homepage: improved predictability of delivery by meeting weekly customer commits, with linearity key to meeting commits consistently.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. They are already staffing the fab-wide constraint Flex Global publishes against.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining TAM
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM semiconductor manufacturer: visible Ops Manager, Production Director, Fab Manager, or Industrial Engineer, and none of the keywords above.
tiers.pain: They are still in the manufacturer set Mila named. Planning and dispatch still sit in heuristics, so engineers firefight and hidden capacity stays on the floor. Homepage: replace outdated, reactive systems with intelligent, real-time data-driven decision-making. AST blog: heuristic schedulers force at least one industrial engineer full-time onto rule maintenance; AST cuts that workload by at least 50%.
tiers.valueProp: Flexciton is the decision-making layer of the autonomous factory: Planner, Local, and Global. Homepage: 25+ fabs around the world, 40+ experts dedicated to semiconductor manufacturing optimization. AI blog, Jamie Potter, CEO: a full-fab deployment replaced rules-based scheduling and recorded a 75% reduction in manual flow-control transactions. Homepage Cost Reduction use case: better tool utilisation, fewer bottlenecks, lower costs in peaks and downturns.
tiers.dataSource: LinkedIn TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM. Cost versus throughput is the A/B here.

campaigns.name: Capacity Commit Brief
campaigns.strategy: Name the planning / wafer-start req and contrast days of spreadsheet starts with Flex Planner plans updated every 45 minutes
campaigns.overview: Scrape Sales Nav jobs, write to the Ops / Production / IE track, and lead with the start plan they are already staffing that still disagrees with real capacity.

campaigns.name: 10 / 30 Planner variant
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 1 list, KPI copy instead of commit copy
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{named_keyword}} in the notice line. Swap the poke to 10% cycle time at any given WIP and 30% less standard deviation from target velocity, Flex Planner page.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the Capacity Commit Brief. Same exclusive route, Planner-by-the-numbers language instead of spreadsheet language.

campaigns.name: Toolset KPI Gap Brief
campaigns.strategy: Name {{named_keyword}} in the open req, then offer objective-based scheduling without rule retune, with 9.4% photo throughput from the homepage
campaigns.overview: The dispatch majority. Toolset name is a merge tag, not a campaign split. Throughput side of Mila's A/B.

campaigns.name: Engineering FTE variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{named_keyword}} in the first line. Lead with Flex Local comparison: legacy dispatch consumes 50% to 80% of one engineering FTE to retune at every fab-state change. Cost side of Mila's A/B.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the KPI Gap Brief. Same exclusive route, FTE language instead of throughput language.

campaigns.name: Timelink Flow Brief
campaigns.strategy: Name the timelink / MES / automation req, then Flex Global connecting local schedulers so timelinks stop becoming scrap
campaigns.overview: The factory-automation side of Anna's autonomous-ops pitch. 29% homepage number is the proof line.

campaigns.name: Seagate commits variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{named_keyword}} in the first line. Lead with Mark Patton at Seagate: weekly customer commits, predictability and linearity on a long cycle-time build.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the Flow Brief. Same exclusive route, delivery language instead of scrap language.

campaigns.name: Autonomous Fab Playbook
campaigns.filter: Remaining in-TAM semiconductor manufacturers, job_keyword_class = none
campaigns.strategy: Notice the manufacturer LinkedIn already lists, name the heuristic-and-firefight gap Mila pitched, offer the playbook of Planner plus Local plus Global. Throughput side of the A/B.
campaigns.overview: Catch-all coverage so every scraped manufacturer still gets one route. The playbook is the tiny yes.

campaigns.name: Cost-reduction variant
campaigns.strategy: Lead with the homepage Cost Reduction use case and the AST blog: workload down by at least 50% versus a full-time engineer on heuristic rules. Do not change routing. Cost side of Mila's original A/B.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the playbook. Still exclusive catch-all, still one TAM.

launchPlan: Pull LinkedIn Sales Nav for semiconductor manufacturers (IDM, foundry, memory, OSAT with a front-end or assembly fab) with a visible Ops Manager, Production Director, Fab Manager, Industrial Engineer, Production Control, or Manufacturing Director, or with production-planning / dispatch / MES jobs. Keep the open-req keyword in the same export. Classify job_keyword_class as planning_capacity, toolset_scheduling, timelink_automation, or none. Suppress already_customer when a Flexciton deployment is visible. Named logos (Seagate, Renesas, Microchip) are not a blanket exclude. The Intel announcement is a partnership, not a customer-wide suppress.

Keyword classes are estimated GTMx taxonomy, not Flexciton site fields. Tune the synonym list after the first Sales Nav pull if a band is starved or overlapping. First match wins. Do not also route on wafer starts, node, headcount, or 'MES not detected'. Those cutoffs are not on flexciton.com, and absence of a MES cookie is unreliable.

Resolve work emails in Apollo only after the domain is routed. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM. Optional careers-page text fills {{fab_area}} (photolithography, diffusion, etch, metrology) as a merge tag only. Optional SEMI / public fab directory is an in_tam gate, not a route.

Launch Tier 1 Capacity Commit Brief first. Smallest list, sharpest starts-versus-capacity signal, closest to Flex Planner (updated every 45 minutes). Commit copy as the control, 10% / 30% Planner KPIs as the A/B on the same list.

Add Tier 2 Toolset KPI Gap Brief once {{named_keyword}} merge tags are clean across dispatch, batching, cycle time, and reticle language. Throughput copy as the control, 50% to 80% of one engineering FTE as the cost A/B. Then Tier 3 Timelink Flow Brief, with Seagate weekly-commits as the delivery A/B.

Turn on the Autonomous Fab Playbook catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM manufacturer still has a route. That is Mila's original Ops / Production pitch. Cost versus throughput is the A/B on this list, not a second TAM. Keep fab_area as a merge tag, not a campaign split, until one job-keyword tier is clearly working.

Account-level TAM is qualitative and almost certainly under the waterfall SOP's 20k-account floor. Flexciton's own autonomous-fab post cites over 100 new wafer fabs expected industry-wide, and the homepage cites 25+ fabs they have already worked with. Volume lives at the contact layer (Ops, Production, IE, production control, per site). Do not print a fake TAM count. Do not launch a tier under about 1,500 contacts. That threshold is the waterfall SOP, not a Flexciton site number. If a keyword band is starved after the scrape, widen synonyms before inventing a headcount cutoff.

thresholds.action: Perfect. Scale that tier. Keep the winning commit, KPI, timelink, or cost variant.
Good. Let it run. Do not mix a non-manufacturer TAM into this waterfall, and do not move the spine onto a raw Apollo semiconductor-Ops list.
Borderline. Swap only the magnet or the first-line job keyword. Do not change the route.

thresholds.rate: Worse than 1 per 500, or reply rate under 1% after 1,500+ sends
thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall. Retune the estimated planning_capacity / toolset_scheduling / timelink_automation synonym lists from the live scrape if a band is starved of contacts.
